title: Teens include 7-year-old Tristan Caron in Urban Air games
excerpt: A group of Milford teenagers invited 7-year-old Tristan Caron, who has autism, to join them at Urban Air Adventure Park in Bellingham, Massachusetts. His mother later found them on Facebook to thank them.
body:
A Facebook search by Tristan Caron’s mother turned up the Milford teenagers who had spent about 40 minutes playing with her 7-year-old son at Urban Air Adventure Park in Bellingham, Massachusetts, according to CBS News Boston.

Earlier this week, Tristan, who has autism, was at the park with his mother, Christina, when the teens noticed him sitting by himself and invited him to play. Livy Molinari told WBZ-TV that the exchange began after she commented on a ball Tristan had just won. “I said ‘that’s a really nice ball you have,’ because he had just won a ball,” she said. “I was like, ‘can I hold it for a second?’ And he was like, ‘yeah sure.’”

From there, the group moved into catch, hide-and-seek and play on the slides. CBS News Boston reported that the teens included Molinari, Kelsey Zozzaro, Anna Held and Kenny Leite, and that they said they did not know Tristan had autism when they invited him to join.

“We just wanted to include him and have a fun time playing around at Urban Air. And I feel really happy he felt included and as joyful as he did,” Held told WBZ-TV, according to CBS News Boston. Zozzaro said, “He was really excited and happy when we asked his mom if he could play with us too.”

Leite said, “It’s nice we included him and other people get to know about this, so maybe they can think about it when other people aren’t included.”

Christina Caron said the moment stood out because her son is not always treated kindly. CBS News Boston reported that she said, “More often than not, he’s not met with kindness,” and later added, “A small act of kindness can really turn someone’s day around. It can change the trajectory, and it just meant so much to me.”

Urban Air Adventure Park has been in contact with everyone involved and plans to invite them back to the park for a day celebrating the teens’ gesture, CBS News Boston reported.

title: Rubio denies pause in Ukraine intelligence-sharing in Uzbekistan
excerpt: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday that the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing used to warn Ukraine about Russian ballistic missile attacks.
body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday in Uzbekistan that the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing meant to warn Kyiv about Russian ballistic missile attacks.

“I don’t know where he’s getting these things from or why he’s saying these things to the press,” Rubio told reporters, according to the New York Post. “There’s been no pause. Zelensky should be focused on bringing an end to this war.”

Those comments came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that U.S. intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches is unique and that Ukraine did not receive it, according to the New York Post’s account of Rubio’s remarks. Rubio’s Monday response in Uzbekistan addressed that complaint directly.

Separately, Rubio has been accusing Ukraine of hitting ships or oil supplies tied to American interests. In an interview released Sunday by Breitbart, he said there had been strikes on energy vessels in the Black Sea and that American companies had called to say “Hey, that was our oil on that ship that was hit by Ukraine,” the New York Post reported.

Rubio added in that interview that he did not believe Ukraine intentionally targeted the ships, but said they had been hit and that the situation added to an already strained energy market. The Post reported that he urged Zelensky to help bring the war to an end.

ABC News separately reported that Rubio made similar claims in a Fox News interview that aired Sept. 22, saying over the previous few months “American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine.” ABC said it was not immediately clear what specific incidents he meant. ABC News also reported that Rubio backed an energy infrastructure ceasefire in that interview, saying it would be “a great idea” if neither side targeted the other’s energy infrastructure.

That earlier Fox News appearance and the Sunday Breitbart interview are separate from Rubio’s Monday remarks in Uzbekistan. In the Sept. 22 interview, Rubio discussed alleged strikes on American-linked ships or oil supplies and said he supported an energy ceasefire. On Monday, he was responding to Zelensky’s complaint about intelligence-sharing, not adding new details about the vessel claim.

The reporting provided so far does not identify the vessels Rubio was referring to or establish that they were U.S.-owned or U.S.-flagged. Kyiv Post reported that Rubio did not name the ships or clarify whether they were American-owned, U.S.-flagged or linked to the United States through cargo, chartering or energy infrastructure.

Kyiv Post said the claim may have referred to vessels using Russia’s Black Sea ports to transport oil connected to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which carries Kazakh crude, but said no public evidence had established that U.S.-owned or U.S.-flagged ships were repeatedly hit. Rubio’s Uzbekistan comments did not add those ship details; they addressed intelligence-sharing and Zelensky’s complaint instead.

Rubio’s remarks come amid continuing friction between Washington and Kyiv over the war and over what kind of U.S. support Ukraine is receiving. Zelensky said on NBC that American intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches is unique and that Ukraine did not receive it, while Rubio insisted Monday that there had been no pause in that warning intelligence.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio alleged that U.S.-linked oil infrastructure has been targeted in recent weeks by Ukraine amid its war with Russia during an interview with Fox News on Tuesday morning, though he conceded it was "probably not" deliberate.

Rubio, who attributed the recent rise in oil prices to conflict in the Black Sea between Russia and Ukraine as well as in Yemen with the Houthis, said in the interview that one of the U.S.'s concerns amid Russia's war was being unintentionally caught in the crosshairs.

"The one thing we are concerned about, however, is that over the last few months, on a number of occasions, American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine.
Ukrainian officials did not immediately respond to ABC News' request for comment about Rubio's claims.

key_facts: Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he was expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia.

His move casts doubt on the likelihood of the White House imposing sanctions on Russia this month, given that a bipartisan law passed by Congress directs the administration to target the top importers of Russian oil and gas.

It also directed Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia's natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.
The U.S. has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned them because of Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, according to the U.S.
The national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. was $6.23 on Friday, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on Sept. 22.
